Q&M to become Medi Lifestyle's second-largest shareholder with deal to sell 60% of EM2AI for $6.76 mil
article:
Medi Lifestyle plans to take a majority stake of 60% in EM2AI, which is now a subsidiary of Q & M Dental Group (Singapore).

Under terms of a non-binding term sheet, the $6.76 mil deal will be paid by issuing 138 million shares to Q&M at 4.9 cents per share.

Upon completion, Q&M will be Medi Lifestyle's second-largest shareholder.

As indicated in its most recent FY2025 annual report, Medi Lifestyle's single largest shareholder is an entity called Lingholm Holdings, which holds around 236.8 million shares, equivalent to a stake of 62.62%.

EM2AI is described as an entity focused on AI-based tools for dental diagnostics and treatment planning.

The technology is deployed to analyse dental X-rays, automating dental charting and generating structured information for dentists to review when planning treatment.

See also: SpaceX completes US$60 bil acquisition of AI start-up Cursor

Medi Lifestyle says this proposed acquisition helps it enter technology-enabled healthcare which can be used beyond the Q&M network.

"We see an opportunity to combine EM2AI’s dental and engineering capabilities with Medi Lifestyle’s capital base, operating support and regional ambitions," says Medi Lifestyle's CEO Tan Lee Seng.

As described in its annual report, Medi Lifestyle now runs a chiropractic and physiotherapy centre at Petaling Jaya and it is also in the business of distributing cell-therapy products and advanced cell-derived beauty solutions in Malaysia.

See also: Anthropic said in talks to buy AI startup Decart for US$6 bil — Bloomberg

Under terms of the deal, there will be a profit-target mechanism set at not less than $1 mil for FY2027 and $1.5 mil for FY2028 and further raised to $2.5 million for FY2029.

In addition, Medi Lifestyle has committed to raising at least $30 million in new capital within two years following completion of the deal to fund EM2AI’s subsequent business activities, including growth in Singapore and Southeast Asia.

Medi Lifestyle shares last traded at 5.4 cents. It is up 440% year to date.

title: Hong Kong’s first-half air passenger traffic up 11.7%, financial secretary says
article:
(Aug 16): Hong Kong’s airport passenger traffic jumped 11.7% on year in the first half, as the Asian financial hub hosted a variety of events and attracted more visitors, according to the city’s Financial Secretary Paul Chan.

Hong Kong is consolidating and enhancing its status as an international aviation hub, he wrote in a blog on Sunday. In the first six months of this year, the Hong Kong International Airport handled over 200,000 aircraft movements, up 4.4% from a year earlier, while passenger traffic reached 32.8 million, Chan added.

The number of visitors to the city reached 31.2 million in the first seven months of 2026, up 12% on year, he wrote. The continuous influx has injected greater vitality into Hong Kong and brought more business opportunities, he added.

Chan wrote in his blog last week that Hong Kong expects more than 1.85 million visitors to attend over 100 events in the second half of the year, generating about HK$5.9 billion in spending and HK$3.3 billion in economic value.
